thread.title: UAA hockey opens a new season and era by taking on the reigning national champs
thread.title_full: UAA hockey opens a new season and era by taking on the reigning national champs

author: adndotcom
title: UAA hockey opens a new season and era by taking on the reigning national champs
text:
The Seawolves have launched their first year under head coach Eric Rud, and will take the ice this weekend against the University of Denver.
The University of Alaska Anchorage hockey team technically took the ice for the first time under new head coach Eric Rud last weekend with a pair of exhibition games.
However, their first real test and first games that actually matter will be held Friday at 7 p.m. and Saturday at 5 p.m. in one of Alaska’s most historic hockey venues, Sullivan Arena.
“This facility is awesome,” Rud said. “There’s been so many special moments in this rink that we’re just happy to be a part of it this weekend. We’re really looking forward to some great fan support, and I know our guys are really excited to put on a great effort. ” The new-look Seawolves will take on reigning NCAA national champion the University of Denver in a two-game series for the second year in a row.
It’s as daunting a home opener as any team in the nation could face, but Rud and his players are looking forward to relishing the challenge.
“Whenever you got the defending national champs coming to town, it definitely gets your spirits up, and it’s exciting,” he said. “This is why our guys came here. They want to play against the best competition in the country, and there’s no better than No. 1 coming in here. ” The Pioneers are coached by Anchorage’s David Carle, who has led the program to national titles in three of the past five seasons.
“They have a bunch of talent and they’re very well coached, and it’s a great team,” Rud said. “It’ll be an awesome challenge for our guys to start the season. ” The two of them go way back to Rud’s days as a recruiter at St. Cloud State University, at a time when Carle was a player looking for a home at the next level.
“From that moment, we’ve always had a really good relationship,” Rud said. “He was at Denver when I was at Colorado College as an assistant. He was just starting as a student coach at that time, really learning the game, so I spent a lot of time around him. ” Rud was still recruiting when Carle was “getting his feet wet” as assistant coach for the Green Bay Gamblers in the United States Hockey League from 2012 to 2014.
“I’ve known him forever, and obviously he’s a tremendous coach, but even a better person,” Rud said. “ just an awesome guy to have around college hockey, and I’m really thankful that he’s not only an enemy on the ice, but we’re friends away from things. I’m really happy for all that he’s done in his career so far.
” Last Halloween, UAA pulled off a major upset when the Seawolves traveled to Colorado and beat Denver 4-3 in the first matchup of a two-game series, notching one of the most notable wins since the program was reinstated in 2022. Senior forward Aiden Westin was the first of three Seawolves players to score a goal in last year’s big road win.
“It was huge to get an upset against him, and we’re hoping to do it again this year, and hopefully I can score another,” Westin said. The former Anchorage Wolverine is excited to not only take on the Pioneers again but also to do it on the home ice of his hometown NAHL franchise.
“We’re excited, especially to play here, got the reigning national champions coming back, but it’s a new year, a new team,” Westin said. “I think we have a chance to take them down. ” With new faces on both the roster and at the helm of the coaching staff, he believes that this team is hungry and determined to make a statement when they take the ice this weekend.
“Obviously it’s a tough opponent, but everybody’s kind of in the same boat for the first game here,” Westin said. “They don’t know what to expect from each other, so we’re gonna go out and try to take it from them. ” Taking stock of early returns Last Friday, UAA skated to a 4-3 win over Mount Royal. Westin scored the game-winner in the fourth round of a shootout.
The Seawolves followed it up on Saturday with a 7-1 win over the University of Mary, with five players each recording a goal and an assist.
“It was nice to get our feet under us,” Westin said. “Obviously, don’t count towards anything, but it was still pretty good competition. I think it prepared us well for this upcoming weekend. ” Exhibition games signal a return to the ice after a long summer, and also give coaching staff opportunities to play several players in different spots as well.
“It felt really good to get some game action in last weekend, and that’s carried over to a really good week of practice,” Rud said. “Guys have been very sharp; we’ve got a lot of stuff done very excited going into this weekend. ” After he was hired to replace former Seawolf legend Matt Shasby in late April, Rud and his staff got busy putting together this year’s roster, including adding 15 players.
They used the transfer portal as well as the junior hockey and high school pipelines to replenish their ranks, but the leadership from older players has helped bring the group closer together. Some players even approached Rud unprompted and shared the observation, “This is one of the closest teams I’ve ever been around,” according to Rud.
“That is total credit to our older guys, our captains, our leaders have just done an amazing job since day one, making sure the school has been ready every day for practice,” Rud said. “Everything we do, they’re chomping at the bit, ready to go, and the rest of the guys have followed. ” With so many new faces, the players have been intentional about spending time together outside the rink and off the ice to strengthen their connections.
“Every weekend, we’ve had some team bonding stuff, going camping and stuff, which has brought us all together,” Westin said. “I think we got a really good group, and everybody takes care of each other. So yeah, we’re good there. ”
